mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5pp in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% year-over-year, the real interest rate is negative, which typically leads to increased investment in equities and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 45% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a quarter, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% in a quarter and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.
